threat_internal_label: food price shock (never shown on screen)
analog: 2008 global rice price crisis (export bans and panic buying amid record harvests)
t0: 2007-10-09 (India stops non-basmati rice exports; month from s1, day assumed)

sources.title: Slayton T., Rice Crisis Forensics: How Asian Governments Carelessly Set the World Rice Market on Fire, Center for Global Development Working Paper 163 (2009)
Timmer C.P., Japan and a Solution to the World Rice Crisis, Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus (2008)
Slayton T., Timmer C.P., Japan, China and Thailand Can Solve the Rice Crisis, but U.S. Leadership is Needed, CGD Notes (May 2008)
IRRI Rice Today: The 2008 rice crisis: fluke or warning bell?
USDA ERS: Factors Behind the Rise in Global Rice Prices in 2008 (RCS-09D-01)

points.notes: 'around $300 in November 2007' is from a secondary summary; confirm against s6

points.event: early-mid May 2008 peak: more than $1,100/t (Thai quote cited by s3; 5% white peaked $1,022 per s2)

threat.notes: extent = share of the price climb from ~$300/t to the ~$1,100/t peak ((price-300)/800). Prices are export quotes for Thai rice; grades differ slightly between sources (5% vs 100%B), so treat mid-points as +/- a few percent. Key context (s2, s1): global production was at record highs and stocks were adequate: the shock was driven by export restrictions and panic buying, not a harvest failure.

fragments.had: >1.5 million tonnes of unwanted imported (WTO minimum-access) rice
the unmet need; a tender withdrawn for lack of supply at high prices
the idea: release Japan's stock to calm the market

fragments.who: Japan + Philippines (+ US consent under WTO rules)
fragments.had: the deal to export the stored rice

fragments.notes: launched Sep 2011; not confirmed in a snippet this pass

aggregation.notes: Derived from documented dates (weeks after India's Oct 2007 ban), not a measured distribution: p10 = importer's need becomes public (failed tender, April 2008), median = Japan-Philippines deal (mid-May 2008), p90 = standing G20 transparency system (Sep 2011, unverified). The stock that fixed it sat in warehouses the whole time.

deploy.notes: Mid-May deal to ~$800/t by June (~4.4 weeks). The announcement itself moved prices; little of the rice needed to ship (per s3's argument; volumes shipped not confirmed).

ai_counterfactual.basis: Illustrative and modest. Matching a public, stated shortage (the withdrawn tender) with a known, idle stock and drafting the terms is a short analysis-and-routing task inside the ~17.4 h 50% task horizon in RATES.md (METR entry). Assumed: the match is surfaced within 1 week of the need becoming public (week 28.3) instead of ~4 weeks later, with governments still negotiating and deciding. We do not assume AI would have spotted the crisis earlier, which would need data not in RATES.md.
ai_counterfactual.label: illustrative

gap_summary: Prices went from ~$300 to over $1,000 a tonne in about 6 months while 1.5 million idle tonnes sat in warehouses; connecting stock to need took ~31 weeks, and once connected prices fell by more than a quarter within ~4 weeks.
